prospect.name: Anthony Boon
prospect.location: United States; originally from Australia, in the US 20 years
prospect.occupation: Commercial real estate broker; building a second income as a trader
prospect.family_status: Separated ~18 months ago after a ~20-year relationship; 17-year-old daughter currently kept overseas by her mother, active legal fight; his own mother is seriously ill in Australia
prospect.training_background: Lifelong sportsman — rugby into his twenties. Lost ~80 lb about 18 months ago on a self-run '30-30-30' protocol with regular 48-hour to 5-day water fasts. Currently sauna ~6x/week, cold plunges previously for a year, some planks and push-ups; describes the last six months or more as slack.
prospect.medical: Left knee gives way intermittently and tight hips, self-attributed to weak glutes; left shoulder tightness with restricted and undiagnosed range of motion; joint aches he attributes to sugar and stress. Resumed smoking cigarettes and weed about 18 months ago after 16 years off. Describes a previous period of being bloated and depressed. No diagnosed condition, medication or clinician disclosed.

signals: Lost ~80 lb 18 months ago then gave the ground back — 'over the last, I don't six months, I've just... I've been a bit slack'
Explicit regret framing: 'there'd always be that niggling thing inside that's like, you didn't do it'
Wants a former and better self: 'I'd really like to see my best body' and 'I haven't seen my abs since I've, you know, I'm like 16'
Hard season is the cause — separation, custody fight, seven months without commission, relapse into smoking

goals.text: See his best-ever physique and his abs for the first time since his teens
Be 'on' all the time — no sluggishness, no afternoon dips; currently rates energy 5.5/10
Natural full-range movement — free up hips, knees and left shoulder
Be physically capable of playing a game of rugby again at 49
Be in his best physical, mental and emotional shape simultaneously — 'unstoppable'
Take the shot now while the window is open — 'if I don't do it now, when?'

pains.text: Nutrition has collapsed — gluten and sugar back in, 'I'm a reward eater', not cooking
Sets goals and does not stick to them — had an Ironman target, trained, then dropped it; 'weak-minded, weak-willed'
Needs external accountability to hold a routine and no longer has any — 'now I don't have a controlling spouse'
Left knee gives way, hips tight, left shoulder range of motion restricted and undiagnosed
Worst period of his life — daughter withheld overseas, legal fight, mother dying in Australia and he cannot get back
Lifelong people-pleaser who puts himself last and doubts he is allowed a good outcome — 'Am I enough?'
Energy self-rated 5.5 out of 10; back on caffeine and energy drinks after quitting stimulants last year
Seven months without a real estate commission, working restaurant jobs, unpaid bills

objections.raw_quote: Is it just that the six grand is not possible at this second? can't, absolutely. Like, man, I'll show you my bank account, I don't have six grand.
objections.rep_response: Reassured he would not push him into a bad financial position, then ran a partial open wallet — cash available, savings, credit score, credit limit — and on learning there was roughly $1,000 and unpaid bills, stopped and proposed a later start date rather than structuring any plan.

objections.raw_quote: by the 30th of August, I'd have six grand for this
objections.rep_response: Pushed back once on the danger of deferral — 'when you don't make a commitment for yourself, it's so, so, so easy to put it to the next day' — then accepted the timeline and booked a start meeting for 21 August, promising free content in the meantime.

prospect_financials.credit_score: mid 500s self-reported, down from low 700s 18 months ago

evidence: Prospect gave a clear verbal yes to the programme before price — 'No, I would like a new identity. I want a new identity. I need a new identity. And I choose a new identity.'
On hearing $6,000 he did not resist the number — '6K up front... Let's get started, or?'
But he had no money — 'I got a grand in my bank and that's it. And I haven't paid my car for this month or insurance.'

Counter-evidence for a close: the prospect twice offered money he could actually access — '500 bucks I could put down in the next week' and 'if you give me two weeks, I'd come up with a grand' — and the rep declined both.
No payment taken and no payment link sent; the rep booked a calendar invite for 21 August instead — 'Invitation, August 21st. Yep. Yeah, perfect.'
outcome.next_step: Rep sent a YouTube video and some workouts to start on unpaid; start meeting held for 21 August, to be pulled forward if his commercial real estate commission lands sooner.

notable.note: The prospect volunteered a deposit twice ($500 within a week, $1,000 within two weeks) and the rep refused it on the grounds it would be rent money, then pushed the start seven weeks out. That is the opposite of the deposit process the manager coaches in the 07/03 team meeting, and it is the single decision that turned a fully-committed prospect into a seven-week follow-up. Separately, the rep endorsed the prospect's habit of weekly 48-hour-plus water fasts alongside starting a new loaded kettlebell programme, after the prospect himself raised lightheadedness. Roughly five minutes of the call happened on a phone call outside the recording because the prospect's audio failed.

quality.notes: Persistent swapping throughout. Discovery questions appear under the prospect's label repeatedly — the 1-10 energy question at 00:23:52, 'Why do you feel like you didn't stick with that program?' at 00:37:00, and the whole 'I was last' passage at 00:37:44. Long merged blocks also attribute both sides of an exchange to one speaker. Role was read from content throughout: Richard Claessen is the rep, Anthony Boon the prospect.
